Hi Sanjay — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Neha (finance/partner ops) to confirm specifics. Quick answers up front:

- Limits: baseline for our hosted product is 1M/2M/1M; for committed Dedicated contracts we can agree to higher limits (2M/4M/2M) subject to underwriter approval and a small commercial surcharge.
- Additional insured: we can grant Additional Insured status on the CG policy for services related to the Order Form; there are standard endorsement templates we use.
- Waiver/primary: waiver of subrogation is okay in many cases; primary and noncontributory language is ok where insurer will accept — sometimes requires insurer sign-off.
- Retroactive date: for Professional Liability, we typically provide a retroactive date equal to the policy inception date at the time of execution; if historical coverage is required we need to confirm with our carrier.
- COI holder language: we can place Aurelia's address and contact on the COI.

I attached our sample COI and a first-pass redline of the MSA insurance exhibit where I made the additional insured clause explicit. Karthik / Neha — please review the attached and advise on any redlines you'd prefer before I send back to Aurelia.

Olga / team — quick legal take:

1) Additional Insured: we'll agree to an Additional Insured endorsement limited to vicarious liability for services performed under the Order Form. Proposed endorsement language included in the attached redline (see section 5.2). We avoid blanket AI for all claims unrelated to the services.

2) Limits: we can accept 2M/4M/2M for the pilot provided Aurelia confirms it as a pass-through cost in the order form or accepts the small surcharge. If they insist on limiting Redwood to 1M/2M/1M we should negotiate a risk allocation (cap or carve-outs).

3) Primary/noncontributory & waiver: we'll provide primary/noncontributory wording and a waiver of subrogation to the extent permitted by the insurer. We need to confirm if the insurer will issue a Waiver of Subrogation endorsement. If they can't, we can propose contractual risk sharing.

4) Retroactive date/prior acts: for claims-made E&O, we can provide retroactive coverage back to the policy inception date; we cannot represent prior carrier history — if Aurelia requires a retro date that predates Redwood's E&O inception, we'd need to review carrier records.

I flagged optional language for 'certificate holder' and recommended a short clause requiring a COI and delivery of any renewals during the Term.

For procurement: Neha, please confirm estimated surcharge to support 2M/4M/2M (if underwriter okays).

-Karthik

Team — ran numbers with underwriter. Preliminary:

- Upgrading from 1M/2M/1M to 2M/4M/2M increases annual premium by ~18–25% depending on carrier. For the pilot (estimated $XXk ARR) we can absorb up to a 12% surcharge; anything above should be passed to the customer or covered via contract (e.g., Aurelia pays surcharge).
- Additional insured endorsement has negligible marginal cost if requested at bind; the insurer prefers to see the endorsement language prior to issuance.
- Waiver of subrogation is typically fine; primary/noncontributory will require the policy to be rated accordingly but is standard.

Recommendation: offer 2M/4M/2M as an optional upgrade at a stated fee in the Order Form (line item). Provide Additional Insured for services with the endorsement attached and require COI with each renewal.
